corrections.why: The Virginia DHR register entry places the station in Hampton (Ind. City); Norfolk County has not existed as a county for decades and the station lies off Hampton at the entrance to Hampton Roads.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 'built 1880, lost' screwpile entry is the second screw-pile house: the first (1872) burned on 30 October 1880 and a house built for Bell's Rock was set on the same foundation and lit 24 December 1880; that house burned in December 1909.

The record's '1914 built / first_lit / deactivated' entries mix two towers. The cast-iron tower went into commission on 1 December 1914; the 'discontinued 1914' in the Archive's screwpile record refers to the screw-pile light, destroyed by fire in 1909 and replaced by a temporary light until 1914.

notes_for_editor: Newspapers: the Chronicling America searches (1909-10, 1880-81) were queued behind other agents' requests and did not return in time, so no newspaper account of the 1880 or 1909 fires is used; the fire accounts rest on Anderson (Lighthousefriends) and the Chesapeake Chapter timeline, which agree. The NRHP nomination (02001436) is not digitised at NPS (placeholder PDF), so the chronology rests on the Commissioner's 1915 'New works completed' entry, Bulletins and secondary sources; the 1872 light's characteristic and first-lighting date (15 Oct 1872) are from Anderson only, because the Lighthouse Board reports for 1872-73 and 1880-81 are not in the corpus. Columns read by position: the 1919 Bulletin efficiency-flag table (Thimble Shoal, Va. ... Horace C. Groom, adjacent in the OCR); the 1918 Bulletin item naming Groom and Preston (OCR garbled: 'Benjamin D. n . C. Groom, keeper , and l'J'C's ton, second assistant'; Preston is the roster's 1918 second assistant); the 1920 Bulletin Feb. 4 storm item, where two printed columns are interleaved in the OCR (I reassembled the sentences by reading across, and the year is taken from the 1920 volume, not printed with the date). The 1926 Bulletin prints three keepers' letters (Hooper Island, Ragged Point, Thimble Shoal) without saying which is which; the 'good sermon' letter is assigned to Thimble Shoal only by Anderson, and the story says so. Disagreements: Twiford's term is 1920-1931 (Archive) versus 1920-1930 (Lighthousefriends), Tillett 1931 versus 1930; Lighthousefriends also lists John M. Beals as head keeper 1956-at least 1957, absent from the Archive roster and not used. The 1927 Bulletin gives the burning of the screw-pile as 190(), the digit damaged; Commissioner 1915, Anderson and the Chesapeake Chapter give 1909. Anderson says the 1873 lens sent red and blue flashes down the avenue; the 1927 Bulletin says red and white, which the story follows. The Commissioner's 1915 report gives the light as occulting (fixed white one second, eclipse one second) and visible 13 miles (units not stated), reed-horn fog signal; Lighthouse Digest gives a white flash every 10 seconds today (record: Fl W 10s); the current optic is the Coast Guard's solar RB 355 per the Archive and Lighthouse Digest. Anderson says a five-foot diaphone was the original fog signal; the 1915 report and Bulletin say reed horn first, changed to diaphone by 1919. Lighthouse Digest's database entry also says '1891: second screwpile structure', which conflicts with Anderson (second house 1880) and was not used. The Archive's position (37 00.49 N, 76 14.26 W, about 0.74 km from the record) is only to the minute; the record's position agrees with Anderson. The Fresnel lens at Yorktown is from Anderson ('a fourth-order Fresnel lens used in Thimble Shoal Lighthouse'); it is not stated to be the 1914 lens or the screw-pile lens. The Strongwell page is a supplier's case study, used only for the fiberglass strut repair. Peter Jurewicz is named as the 2005 buyer as printed by Lighthouse Digest and Anderson. Keepers: the whole roster comes from the Archive (cite 12 for the screw-pile place, 1872-1914; cite 1 for the cast-iron tower, 1912-1964); roster names for the years 1912-1914 appear under both places in the Archive; Charles S. Hudgins (1910-1914) is listed as screw-pile head keeper although that house burned in December 1909. 'Alexander G. Lee' (Archive) and 'A. J. Lee' (Brown's letter, via Anderson) are treated as one person. Roster 'person' slugs are the roster.py slugs for each line. USCG lines are Coast Guard crew; Austin appears as USCG 1947-48 and as head keeper 1948-49 (one person per the Archive). The story says 'a head keeper and two assistants' from the roster pattern; the 1915 report confirms quarters for three keepers.
